$description: The axis grid and the token-set version. Borrows the shape of the DTCG Resolver Module (sets, modifiers, named contexts, an explicit resolution order) without adopting its file format, because that module is a draft carrying the instruction not to implement it. If it stabilises unchanged, this becomes a serialisation change.

tokenSet.bumpPolicy: MAJOR when a token is removed or its meaning is redefined; MINOR when a token is added or deprecated; PATCH for a value change that alters no binding.
tokenSet.bindsFromNote: Forward-only. A screen ratified under 2.0.x remains conformant to 2.0.x; a bump does not reopen it. Same rule the project constitution uses for its own principles.
tokenSet.changeClassNote: The producer's claim, not a verified property. Nothing checks it. There is no classified taxonomy of breaking design changes to check it against — the equivalent for an API contract has 509 rules, and for tokens the state of the art is a diffing plugin.

platform.description: Selects token values, component set and interaction model — which is why it is an axis and not a theme.

macos.baselineNote: Never verified. Recorded as null rather than omitted, so the gap is visible instead of absent.

tvos.reason: A converter is entered a digit at a time and read once. On a focus-engine remote that is worse than useless, and nobody asked for it. Declined explicitly so the grid records a decision rather than an omission.

coverage.note: The grid is combinatorial and most cells are uninteresting. Only cells that differ materially are authored; the rest resolve from the defaults. A cell is recorded here when it was considered and found not to differ, so silence never has to mean two things.
consideredAndIdentical: ipados × dark × regular — identical to ios × dark once the layout resolves
macos × light × regular — identical to ipados × light × regular apart from the input model
